worksheet.title: The Wrong Turn
worksheet.subtitle: Ontario Math C3.2 — read, find, and fix code
worksheet.learning_goal: I can fix a turtle shape loop with the wrong turn angle.

parts.title: Wrong turn, open shape
text: In a turtle shape, each shape needs the right turn: square 90, triangle 120, pentagon 72, hexagon 60.
If the turn is wrong, the shape will not close. The range can be right and it still looks wrong — check the turn.

parts.title: This should draw a TRIANGLE — but it's buggy
parts.output: The corners are wrong — the triangle does not close.

parts.caption: right 90 won't make a triangle; right 120 closes it.

parts.title: Find the bug
parts.prompt: The triangle code uses right(90). A triangle needs right 120. What should right() be? ______

parts.title: Fix the hexagon
parts.prompt: This should draw a hexagon (6 sides):  for i in range(6): bit.forward(40); bit.right(90). A hexagon needs right 60. What is wrong, and what should the turn be?

parts.title: Write the fix
parts.prompt: Bit should draw a pentagon (5 sides). The turn for a pentagon is 72. Write it:  bit.right(______)

parts.title: Challenge
parts.prompt: A SQUARE loop has right(60) instead of right(90). Will the square close? Why not? What should the turn be?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Each shape has its own turn. If the shape does not close, the turn is probably wrong — match the turn to the shape (square 90, triangle 120, …).

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students debug turtle shape loops where the TURN angle is wrong so the shape will not close (C3.2). Correct angles are given (square 90, triangle 120, pentagon 72, hexagon 60).

parts.title: Curriculum (Ontario Math 2020, Strand C3)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: Python Turtle projected (or a web playground); a turn chart (square 90, triangle 120, pentagon 72, hexagon 60); worksheet + pencil per student.

parts.title: Run it (about 30 min)
text: 1. Run the triangle with right(90) — the open/odd shape shows the bug.
2. Change to right(120); it closes. Post the turn chart for the shapes.
3. Students do Exercises 1–4 (Ex 4 is the stretch), solo or in pairs.
4. Share answers; land the big idea: if it won't close, fix the turn.

parts.title: Answer key (checked by the run-gate)
text: Ex 2 — the turn is wrong; change right(90) to right(60).
Ex 4 (challenge) — no, it will not close; right(60) is a hexagon turn. Use right(90) for a square.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: changing the range when the TURN is the bug.
Support: give the turn chart and have students match shape → turn.
Extend: ask the turn for an octagon if it does not close (45).

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The student recognises an unclosed shape as a wrong-turn bug and fixes the angle to match the shape (Ex 1–3), explaining why a mismatched turn fails (Ex 4).
